hook.line: 33 holes and 32 marbles. Jump, take, and see if you can leave the last one in the middle.
hook.say: Bonjour! Let me show you the story of peg solitaire.

ch.t: From the court of Louis XIV
ch.say: The first record dates from 1697 — it was born in France!
p: The oldest record of peg solitaire comes from France in 1697. It was played at the court of Louis XIV, and in August that year the magazine Mercure galant described the board, the rules and some problems. An engraving from the same year shows the Princess of Soubise with the board beside her.

In 1710 the German philosopher Leibniz wrote about the game in a Berlin learned journal, and in Britain it settled in under the name “solitaire”. In the 20th century it became a subject for mathematicians, and in America a triangle board became a fixture on restaurant tables.

ch.say: Just one rule — and yet so deep!
ch.cap: The English 33-hole board: only the middle starts empty, and on the first move the right-hand marble jumps its neighbour into the middle
p: A marble jumps over a neighbouring marble, up, down or sideways, into the empty hole just beyond. The marble jumped over is taken off the board. The same marble may keep jumping.
When no marble can jump, the game is over. Leave just one marble to succeed — on the chosen hole (usually the middle) for a perfect game.
